timeline.label: 1 June · passed
timeline.title: New-party application deadline
timeline.description: The VEC cannot accept late applications for registration for the 2026 election.

timeline.label: 21 October
timeline.title: Prepare the forms
timeline.description: Candidate Helper is now available to prepare nomination forms; it does not lodge a nomination. Formal nominations open 4 November.

timeline.label: 3 November · 8 pm
timeline.title: Enrolment closes
timeline.description: Writs issue that day. Check enrolment before the roll closes.

timeline.label: 4-7 November
timeline.title: Nomination appointments
timeline.description: Nominations open 4 November at 9 am. Independent appointment hours: 4-6 November, 9-5; 7 November, 9-1.

timeline.label: 9 November · noon
timeline.title: Nominations and Council grouping closed
timeline.description: Nominations closed at noon AEDT on 9 November.

timeline.label: 10 November
timeline.title: VEC publishes the ballot field
timeline.description: The VEC confirmed 1,037 candidates: 734 for the Legislative Assembly and 303 for the Legislative Council.

timeline.label: 18-27 November
timeline.title: Early voting
timeline.description: Early voting in Victoria runs 18–27 November, 9 am–6 pm AEDT. Centres are closed on Sunday 22 November.

timeline.label: 19 November
timeline.title: VEC statement on Richmond early voting
timeline.description: The VEC said an unauthorised person worked under supervision at Richmond’s Victoria Street early voting centre on 18 November after appointment checks were missed. It said vote integrity was maintained. As a precaution, sealed boxes containing about 700 in-district votes will be tracked into the count as a separate parcel.

timeline.label: 20 November · noon AEDT
timeline.title: How-to-vote card registration closed
timeline.description: The VEC confirms the registration period has closed. Voters can consult the official register and choose their own preferences.

timeline.label: 25 November · 6 pm AEDT
timeline.title: Postal vote applications close
timeline.description: Use the VEC’s postal voting page for the application and instructions for voting within or outside Victoria.

timeline.label: Weekdays through 27 November · Perth
timeline.title: Victorian voting at WAEC in Perth
timeline.description: Eligible Victorian voters in Western Australia can vote at the WA Electoral Commission, Level 2, 66 St Georges Terrace, Perth. The published weekday hours are 8:30 am–4:30 pm, Perth local time, through Friday 27 November. Check the official notice for venue details.

timeline.label: 28 November · 8-6
timeline.title: Election day
timeline.description: Voting centres in Victoria open 8 am–6 pm AEDT. Victoria elects its Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council.

timeline.label: 28 November · before 6 pm AEDT
timeline.title: Post or drop off a completed postal vote
timeline.description: The VEC says to post the completed vote or hand it in at a Victorian voting centre before this cutoff. Overseas voters should check the VEC’s separate return options.

timeline.label: 4 December · 6 pm AEDT
timeline.title: VEC receipt cutoff for postal votes
timeline.description: The VEC must receive the postal vote by this date and time for it to be considered for counting.

timeline.label: 19 December
timeline.title: Scheduled writ return
timeline.description: The formal timetable extends beyond polling day.

stateSummary.researchStatus: 13 November: verified the VEC nomination totals, candidate directory and voting timetable for the 28 November state election. Focused 9 November Baird Ward timetable check: Knox confirms election day 6 February 2027 and postal voting close 5 February at 6 pm AEDT. Rolls close 25 November at 4 pm; nominations run 14–22 December, closing noon. Peter Lockwood resignation evidence retains its 31 October check. Kinglake, Parliament and campaign records retain their earlier reviews.
stateSummary.governmentNote: Ben Carroll was sworn in as Premier on 28 July 2026. The next state election is scheduled for 28 November 2026.

election.label: 2026 Victorian State election
election.note: The VEC confirmed 1,037 candidates on 10 November: 734 Assembly and 303 Council. Nominations closed at noon on 9 November. Early voting in Victoria runs 18–27 November, 9 am–6 pm, with centres closed on Sunday 22 November. Election day voting is 28 November, 8 am–6 pm. All times are AEDT. See the VEC candidate directory under Sources.
